subject: Pricing alignment & migration proposal for Starlite
messages:
From: Alan Dunne <alan.dunne@starlite.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@starlite.ai
Date: 2027-08-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Pricing alignment & migration proposal for Starlite

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for taking this — we’re coming up on our renewal with CloudSpan and I wanted to give you early visibility. Starlite has been evaluating runtime and unit-costs across a couple of vendors; CloudSpan has landed us an aggressive renewal offer and I wanted to see if Redwood can match that footprint + provide a migration assistance package.

High level:
- Current committed spend: ~$1.2M annualized (runtime + embeddings).
- CloudSpan renewal: 18% discount off list + $60k migration credit + 6-week free pilot window.
- Key asks from our side: price parity for first 12 months (or equivalent credits), a clear migration plan (estimated hands-on effort), and confirmation on embedding storage/retention SLAs.

We’re not asking for a one-size-fits-all yet — would like to see a concrete offer we can take to procurement. I’ve attached a short extracts package from our RFP and the incumbent renewal term for context (starlite-rfp-extracts.pdf).

Can we get a preliminary commercial outline by Tuesday? Happy to take a 30–45m call with your solutions lead if helpful.

Best,
Alan Dunne
Head of Procurement, Starlite AI
alan.dunne@starlite.ai
procurement@starlite.ai

Hi Alan — thanks for the details and the attachment. I’m looping in Jordan (account lead) so he can see the incumbent terms and we can draft an offer that lines up to your expectations. A few clarifying Qs to speed a proposal:

1) Is the $60k migration credit a one-time cash credit applied to invoices or an engineering services credit?
2) Do you have an expected go-live window if the commercials are agreed (target month)?
3) Are there any hard compliance requirements beyond standard data retention (e.g., special encryption/hsm processes)?

Initial thought: we can typically match price parity via a combination of an up-front migration credit + a stepped discount during year-1. I’ll attach a short econ outline to frame options.

Available for a call tomorrow 2–4pm PT if that suits — happy to set up a solutions deep-dive to run the migration plan and scope.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Attachments: draft-econ-outline.pdf (1 page)
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Alan Dunne <alan.dunne@starlite.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-30T08:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing alignment & migration proposal for Starlite

Alan — appreciate the context. We ran the numbers and here’s a runnable commercial we can take to your procurement team. I’m copying Laura from legal for heads-up on contract mechanics.

Commercial outline (prelim):
- Price: 15% off our published runtime + embedding list rates for the first 12 months.
- Migration credit: $50,000 applied as service credits toward onboarding; can convert to invoice credit on acceptance.
- Pilot: 4-week pilot environment (no charge) with technical support hours included (up to 40h).
- Commit: 12-month minimum term with monthly invoicing; 12% uplift on overages thereafter.

Conditions and notes:
- Pricing contingent on a 12-month committed minimum and completion of a short migration SOW (scope to be confirmed during technical kickoff).
- We can include an explicit rollback/fallback window in the SOW for the first 30 days after Go-Live.

I can approve up to 20% discount with manager sign-off if the procurement team needs it — for the purpose of getting you to an internal yes, we’ll offer the 15%/50k package above as our standard match.

I’ve attached a short term-sheet that captures the headline economics and gating items (starlite-term-sheet-v1.pdf). If Starlite is comfortable we can push a DocuSign the same week.

Next steps (recommended):
1) Confirm whether the migration credit should be invoice credit or services credit.
2) Accept headline terms so we can spin up the pilot environment and schedule a technical kickoff (I propose Sept 9 or 10).
3) Procurement to send any redlines — Laura will coordinate on the legal side.

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
jordan_blake@redwood.com

Attachments: starlite-term-sheet-v1.pdf (2 pages)
From: Alan Dunne <alan.dunne@starlite.ai>

Date: 2027-09-02T15:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing alignment & migration proposal for Starlite

Jordan / Marissa — thanks for moving quickly. Starlite is prepared to accept the 15% discount + $50k migration credit as outlined, subject to a short SOW that confirms milestones and the post-go-live rollback window. Procurement prefers the migration credit to be applied as an invoice credit.

Two asks before we finalize:
- Can you share the DocuSign link for the term-sheet/contract?
- Can the technical kickoff be scheduled for Sept 9 at 10am PT (internal engineers are available then)?

If we get those, I’ll route the DocuSign and our standard PO process. Looking forward to getting this moving.

Best,
Alan Dunne
Head of Procurement, Starlite AI
